text:
Sam W: Heads-up — Procurement forwarded an InvoiceIQ demo this morning. They claim ML/cloud invoice parsing + normalized cost mapping for LLM/token usage. anyone saw the deck?
Priya N: I skimmed. Looks promising for line-item normalization. Key Q: can they map to our model-level buckets (model, route, env)?
Marcus L: Important: we need attribution to route/model + reserved capacity amortization. Many vendors collapse all GPU charges into single blob = useless.
Avery C: Also need embedding/token-level splits. Our billing ties tokens -> customer route, embeddings -> separate SKU. Can InvoiceIQ split on same invoice? :thinking_face:
procurement-bot: InvoiceIQ quoted a POC: 4 weeks, ingest of 3 months of invoices, up to 4 providers, flat $6k trial fee (one-time).
Elaine S: What about security/compliance? we can't send raw invoice PDFs with customer PII off-platform unless they support SSO + KMS + retention controls.
Sam W: Good catch. Priya, can you ask for their security datasheet and whether they support customer-managed keys?
Priya N: Yep. I'll ping them. Also asking for: delta accuracy score (line-item to cost-center), support for templates + custom rules, and whether they output canonical CSV + JSON with our schema.
Marcus L: If they can output a normalized CSV that includes: invoice_date, invoice_id, line_item_description, provider, service, units, unit_type, cost, cost_center, model_tag, route_tag — that'll make our reconcile pipeline simple.
Avery C: sample CSV I'd expect:
```
date,invoice_id,line_item,provider,service,units,unit_type,cost,cost_center,model
2026-02-01,INV-234,EC2 Spot GPU hours,aws,ec2,12.5,Hrs,150.00,infra,gpt-4o
```
Priya N: Sent them our minimal schema + asked for sample transform of 2 invoices. Requested SLA around mapping accuracy and turnaround for exceptions.
procurement-bot: Vendor replied: supports SSO (SAML/OIDC), customer KMS for attachments, retention policies, and redaction. They offered test dataset anonymization.
Elaine S: Good. Pricing model? per-invoice or per-GB processed? POC fee is one thing, but recurring cost needs to scale with our monthly invoice volume (we have ~1200 lines/month across providers).
Sam W: We should also ask for support on credits/refunds and reserved commit amortization across months. Those are huge for Dedicated billing.
Marcus L: Another ask: can they link cost lines back to API request IDs or traces? Not mandatory, but helpful for high-fidelity chargebacks.
Avery C: If they can't do request-level, at least allow joining via our tags (model, cluster, route) based on line-item heuristics.
Priya N: Vendor said they can run rule-engine + ML classifier to tag items; accuracy ~92% out-of-the-box, 97% after training on our labeled set. They can do custom rules for reserved amortization.
Sam W: Sounds reasonable. Let's scope POC acceptance criteria: 1) parse 3 months, 95% model/route tagging accuracy on a 300-line sample 2) normalized csv matching our schema 3) SSO + KMS confirmed 4) sample reconciliation script showing month-over-month commit amortization.
Elaine S: Add: show how credits/refunds are applied (line-level vs invoice-level) and provide an explanation for any unmapped lines.
procurement-bot: Action: Priya to coordinate POC kickoff, Marcus to upload anonymized invoices to S3 (bucket link), Avery to provide expected schema and a small labeled sample (50 lines) for training.
Marcus L: I'll drop sample set: s3://redwood-internal/procurement/invoiceiq-poc/ — will anonymize account IDs first. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Avery C: I'll export labeled csv and put in the same bucket. quick note: label field name = model_tag, route_tag, cost_center.
Priya N: Scheduled vendor kickoff for Mon 10am PT. Asked them to share a draft statement of work and POC acceptance criteria by Friday. :thumbsup:
Sam W: If POC looks good, target is product-level integration in Redwood Console (show normalized cost per route/model). That's a product ask — will loop in Eng once POC passes.
Elaine S: Finance will need cost forecasts impact — ask vendor if they provide trend dashboards or only raw outputs.
Priya N: They offer both: raw normalized files + an optional dashboard. Dashboard is extra; we asked for export-first approach.
Marcus L: FYI, flagged question: can they handle multi-currency invoices and FX adjustments? Vendor said yes, with base currency normalization and audit trail.
Avery C: One last thing — retention: we need to keep raw parsed JSON for at least 7 years for audit. Can they export to our S3 on a schedule?
procurement-bot: Vendor: supports periodic S3 export and offboarding data dump. Also supports webhooks for real-time emits.
Sam W: Great. Priya — please post vendor security docs and the draft SOW in the procurement channel when you have them. We'll review and decide whether to proceed with POC.
Priya N: Will do. Thanks all. :v:
